name: Nationality by Descent / Birth

requirement_groups.name: Child of an Algerian father or mother

requirements.blocker_text: Code de la Nationalite Algerienne, Article 6: 'Est considere comme Algerien l'enfant ne de pere algerien ou de mere algerienne' -- a child born to either an Algerian father or an Algerian mother is Algerian, explicitly gender-neutral.

requirement_groups.name: Born in Algeria to unknown parents

requirements.blocker_text: A child born in Algeria to unknown parents is presumed Algerian. If paternity or maternity is later established as belonging to a foreign national, the child may instead acquire that foreign nationality and lose Algerian status -- a conditional, reversible presumption rather than an unconditional jus soli grant.

sources.title: Wikipedia (French) -- Algerian nationality, quoting Code de la Nationalite Algerienne Article 6 (descent) and the conditional jus soli rule for foundlings

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Algeria). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to Wikipedia (tier 4, though it directly quotes the code's article text), since a Journal Officiel or other government-hosted primary text was not successfully fetched in this build (private legal-hosting sites carrying the full code returned fetch errors). GENUINE, GENDER-NEUTRAL FINDING: Article 6's explicit 'pere algerien ou mere algerienne' phrasing carries no asymmetry -- see dz_citizenship_by_marriage.json's notes for a related but distinct finding on the marriage-acquisition provision's own gender language. DISTINCTIVE, CONDITIONAL JUS SOLI: unlike most countries in this dataset with unconditional territorial birthright citizenship for foundlings, Algeria's presumption for a child born to unknown parents can be REVERSED if a foreign parent is later identified -- a real, disclosed limitation rather than an unconditional safeguard. dual_citizenship_allowed left null: no source reviewed in this build addressed Algeria's general dual-nationality policy.
